_meta.purpose: Derived vs experimental masses for every particle that has an FTD formula. Source: scripts/constants.py + scripts/proofs/proof_complete_sm.py. Experimental values: PDG 2024.
_meta.units: MeV unless noted; GeV marked with _GeV suffix
_meta.epistemic: Every 'formula' below is [THEOREM] that produces a *ratio* from framework integers. The absolute scale is fixed by [IMPOSED] m_e = 0.511 MeV = K_B. Do not cite 'mass derivation' without this distinction.

bosons.name: W
bosons.formula: m_W = m_Z * cos(theta_W) = m_Z * sqrt(1 - 3/13) = m_Z * sqrt(10/13)

bosons.name: Z
bosons.formula: m_Z from SU(2) x U(1) Higgs VEV; mass scale via v_Higgs = 246.09 GeV
bosons.note: The FTD derivation fixes sin^2(theta_W) = 3/13 and the ratio m_W/m_Z. The absolute scale requires the Higgs VEV as an input.

open_derivations.note: Mass splitting m_n - m_p ~ 1.29 MeV not yet derived from framework; empirically lifted from PDG.
Pseudoscalar meson mass formulas require chiral perturbation theory; not yet bridged to FTD.

open_derivations.particle: quarks (u, d, s, c, b, t)
open_derivations.note: Top quark mass ~172 GeV ~ v_Higgs supports a Yukawa-at-unity story; light-quark masses and CKM matrix are [OPEN].
